ayuda.title: Luna — Help
ayuda.section1.title: What is Luna?
ayuda.section1.p1: Luna is a remote control system that turns your phone into a wireless extended keyboard for your Windows PC. Unlike generic solutions (such as traditional remote control apps), Luna processes each keypress locally on the computer through a FastAPI server, offering virtually imperceptible latency regardless of your Wi-Fi speed.
ayuda.section1.arch1: The phone sends binary WebSocket packets (KeyCommand or SliderCommand) to the server on the PC.
ayuda.section1.arch2: The FastAPI server receives the packet and deserializes it using the internal protocol (protocol.py).
ayuda.section1.arch3: The keyboard_engine translates the command into a sequence of Win32 events (SendInput, keybd_event).
ayuda.section1.arch4: The key is executed in the active desktop window as if you had physically pressed the keyboard.
ayuda.section1.arch_p: The entire phone → PC pipeline happens in milliseconds. Local audio (MCI) and sliders (volume/brightness/scroll) are controlled through direct Win32 API and ctypes calls, without relying on external services.
ayuda.section1.uc1: Video / Audio editing: Complex keyboard shortcuts (Ctrl+Shift+S, Alt+F4, etc.) without leaving your couch.
ayuda.section1.uc2: Gaming: Programmable keys for MMOs, quick binds in shooters, or combined macros.
ayuda.section1.uc3: Streaming (OBS): Switch scenes, mute microphone, trigger alerts with a single tap from your phone.
ayuda.section1.uc4: Productivity: Specific profiles for Photoshop, VS Code, browser, etc. with automatic profile switching.
ayuda.section2.title: Connection
ayuda.section2.p1: For your phone and PC to communicate, both must be connected to the same local Wi-Fi network. Luna does not use the Internet at any point during key exchange; all traffic is internal (LAN).
ayuda.section2.step1: Run Luna.exe on your Windows PC. A window will open with a loading spinner; in the background, the HTTP/WebSocket server starts on port 9120.
ayuda.section2.step2: Wait for the interface to load (you'll see the control panel with the Luna logo).
ayuda.section2.step3: On your phone, open a browser (Chrome, Firefox, Edge) or the Luna APK.
ayuda.section2.method_a_p: On the PC status bar you'll see a QR icon button. Press it and scan the code with your phone's camera. The QR encodes the address http://{ip}:9120 and will take you directly to the interface.
ayuda.section2.method_b_p: If your phone doesn't have a camera or the QR doesn't work, type directly in the browser:
ayuda.section2.method_b_p2: Replace 192.168.x.x with your PC's local IP. You can see it in the Luna window or by opening Command Prompt (cmd) → ipconfig and looking for the IPv4 Address of your active network adapter.
ayuda.section2.warn_p: If your phone won't connect, the firewall may be blocking port 9120. Open Control Panel → Windows Firewall → Allow an app or feature through the firewall and make sure Luna.exe (or Python) has permissions on private networks. You can also temporarily disable the firewall to confirm.
ayuda.section2.info_p: Windows classifies Wi-Fi networks as "Public" or "Private". On public networks (cafÃ©s, libraries) the firewall blocks device-to-device communication by default. Change the network to Private in Settings → Wi-Fi → Network properties.
ayuda.section3.title: Profiles
ayuda.section3.p1: A profile is a set of buttons (shortcuts) grouped under a name, designed for a specific context or application. For example, you can have a "Photoshop" profile with brush and layer keys, an "OBS" profile for scene switching, and a "Browser" profile for tabs and bookmarks.
ayuda.section3.create1: On the main panel, click the "+" button next to the profile chips.
ayuda.section3.create3: The new profile is created with an empty 4×4 grid (16 buttons).
ayuda.section3.edit_p: Editing is done from the Dashboard (/dashboard). There you can:
ayuda.section3.edit1: Reorder buttons by dragging them to another position.
ayuda.section3.edit2: Edit a button by clicking on it → the editor opens with all fields (label, keyCode, modifiers, icon, sound).
ayuda.section3.edit3: Clear a button using the "Restore profile" button.
ayuda.section3.edit4: Delete the profile ("default" cannot be deleted).
ayuda.section3.switch_p: On the main interface, profiles appear as horizontal chips (pills). Tap one to activate it. The active profile is marked with the accent color (cyan). You can also switch profiles from your phone.
ayuda.section4.title: Key Editor
ayuda.section4.p1: Each button on the grid represents a keyboard shortcut or an action. Clicking a button from the dashboard opens the editor with the following fields:
ayuda.section4.label_p: Visible text shown on the button. Maximum 8 characters to avoid overflow. Examples: "Save", "Copy", "SS".
ayuda.section4.keycode_p: Define which key is pressed and with which modifiers (Ctrl, Alt, Shift, Win).
ayuda.section4.keycode1: KeyCode: Numeric code of the key according to Windows Virtual-Key Codes. You can type the number directly (e.g. 83 = S key) or select from the dropdown menu.
ayuda.section4.keycode2: Modifiers: Select one or more (Ctrl, Alt, Shift, Win). The value is stored as a bitmask that the server interprets to generate the exact combination. Example: Ctrl + Shift + S is represented as KeyCode 83 with modifiers Ctrl|Shift.
ayuda.section4.keycode_hold: For keys without modifiers, the APK uses multi-touch + hold behavior: hold for sustained press, quick tap for single press. Keys with modifiers always execute on tap.
ayuda.section4.icon_p: You can assign a PNG, JPG or GIF image (max. 5 MB) to appear inside the button. Icons are uploaded to the server via the /api/upload-icon endpoint and stored in the custom_icons folder of the data directory. A well-chosen icon speeds up visual recognition of the shortcut.
ayuda.section4.sound_p: Luna can play a local audio file (WAV or MP3) on your PC when you press a button. This uses the Windows MCI (Media Control Interface) engine via ctypes.windll.winmm.mciSendStringW.
ayuda.section4.sound1: Multi-layer: Each sound plays on its own channel (aliases luna_0 to luna_15). You can layer up to 16 sounds simultaneously without them cutting each other off.
ayuda.section4.sound2: Non-blocking: Playback runs in a separate thread (daemon=True), so it doesn't interfere with command reception.
ayuda.section4.tip_p: Assign a short sound (e.g. click.wav) to critical buttons for auditory confirmation that the key was executed. This is especially useful when the phone is out of your field of view.
ayuda.section5.title: Advanced Controls
ayuda.section5.sliders_p: Luna includes a touch slider that you can configure to control different system parameters. When you activate Sliders mode (sliders icon in the mode bar), the key grid is replaced by a horizontal slider control.
ayuda.section5.slider1: System volume: Adjusts the Windows master volume (0-100%). Uses the win32api to modify the audio mixer level.
ayuda.section5.slider2: Screen brightness: Controls monitor brightness via WMI (WmiMonitorBrightnessMethods class). Only works on internal monitors (laptops).
ayuda.section5.slider3: Horizontal scroll: Emulates horizontal scroll wheel events (WM_MOUSEHWHEEL).
ayuda.section5.slider4: Vertical scroll: Emulates the standard mouse wheel.
ayuda.section5.sliders_note: You can change the slider function from the selection menu at the top of the sliders panel.
ayuda.section5.hold_p: The Hold behavior allows you to keep a key pressed continuously without having to hold your finger on the button. It's useful for:
ayuda.section5.hold3: Games that require holding a key (accelerate, walk).
ayuda.section5.hold_note: In the APK, keys without modifiers use multi-touch + hold: quick tap for single press, hold for sustained press. A visual indicator on the button shows if hold is active.
ayuda.section6.title: Auto-switch
ayuda.section6.p1: Auto-switch lets Luna automatically detect which window is active on your PC and switch the phone's profile accordingly, without you having to touch it.
ayuda.section6.how_p: The WindowTracker component runs a background loop that checks the active desktop window every 500 ms using the Win32 GetForegroundWindow API. When it detects that the title or executable of the active window matches a configured profile, it sends a switch_profile message through the WebSocket to the phone.
ayuda.section6.config_p: On the dashboard (/dashboard), you can associate a profile with a specific executable:
ayuda.section6.config2: Select the profile you want to assign.
ayuda.section6.config3: Browse for the application executable (e.g. photoshop.exe, code.exe, chrome.exe).
ayuda.section6.config_note: When focus changes to that application, the phone will automatically switch to the assigned profile. If the active window doesn't match any configured profile, the current profile is kept.
ayuda.section6.perf_p: The 500 ms query is lightweight (one GetForegroundWindow call + title read). It doesn't affect system performance or battery consumption. When no phone is connected, the tracker pauses automatically.
ayuda.section7.title: APK vs Web
ayuda.section7.p1: Luna can be used from any modern browser on your phone, but the Luna APK offers significant advantages for daily use. Here's a detailed comparison:
ayuda.section7.apk1: Full screen: No address bar, no browser chrome. The UI takes up all available space.
ayuda.section7.apk2: Wake lock: The phone screen doesn't turn off while using Luna. No need to tap the screen every N seconds to keep it on.
ayuda.section7.apk3: Native QR scanner: Scan the QR code directly from the app, no third-party apps needed.
ayuda.section7.apk4: Polished navigation: Android's back button integrates with the UI, allowing you to hide/show the interface without reloading.
ayuda.section7.apk5: Automatic updates: The APK periodically checks for a new version on GitHub and offers to download and install it with a single click.
ayuda.section7.web1: No installation: Open the browser, type the URL and you're using Luna. Ideal for a quick test or sporadic use.
ayuda.section7.web2: Cross-platform: Works on iOS, Android, or any device with a modern browser.
ayuda.section7.web3: Limitations: The screen turns off due to system timeout, the address bar takes up valuable space, and there's no integrated QR scanner.
ayuda.section7.recommendation: Recommendation: Use the web version to test Luna for the first few minutes. If you like it, install the APK for a much smoother and more professional experience. You can download it from sr-lolo.github.io/luna.
ayuda.section8.title: FAQ
ayuda.section8.q1: Why won't my phone connect to the PC?
ayuda.section8.a1_1: Firewall blocking port 9120: Make sure Luna.exe or Python has permission on private networks in Windows Firewall.
ayuda.section8.a1_2: Public network: Windows blocks device-to-device communication on public networks. Change the network to "Private" in Settings → Wi-Fi → Properties.
ayuda.section8.a1_3: Same network: Verify both devices are connected to the same router and same band (2.4 GHz or 5 GHz). Some routers isolate clients on the 5 GHz band.
ayuda.section8.a1_4: Wrong IP: Check the IP shown in the Luna window. If it changes frequently, set a fixed IP on your PC from the router or Network Properties.
ayuda.section8.a1_final: If all the above is correct, try accessing from the PC browser at http://127.0.0.1:9120. If it doesn't load, the server didn't start correctly.
ayuda.section8.q2: Why can't I hear sound when pressing a button?
ayuda.section8.a2_intro: The sound plays on the PC, not the phone. Check the following:
ayuda.section8.a2_1: Audio file: Make sure the WAV or MP3 file was uploaded correctly to the server (from the key editor in the dashboard).
ayuda.section8.a2_2: Supported format: Only WAV and MP3. The server rejects other formats with a 400 error.
ayuda.section8.a2_3: PC speakers: Verify that the PC volume isn't muted or too low.
ayuda.section8.a2_4: MCI busy: The MCI engine has 16 available channels. If you exceed that simultaneous limit, additional sounds are silently ignored.
ayuda.section8.q3: How do I minimize Luna without closing it?
ayuda.section8.a3_intro: Luna can run in the background (system tray) while the server stays active for your phone.
ayuda.section8.a3_1: Press the X on the Luna window.
ayuda.section8.a3_2: In the dialog that appears, select "Background".
ayuda.section8.a3_3: The window hides and an icon appears in the system tray (next to the Windows clock).
ayuda.section8.a3_4: To restore the window, double-click the tray icon.
ayuda.section8.a3_5: To close Luna completely, right-click the tray icon and select "Exit", or press X and choose "Close completely".
ayuda.section8.q4: Profiles don't appear or changes aren't saved
ayuda.section8.a4_intro: Profile configuration is stored in a JSON file in Luna's data directory. If changes don't persist:
ayuda.section8.a4_1: Write permissions: Make sure the Windows user has write permissions in Luna's installation directory.
ayuda.section8.a4_2: Corrupt file: If the JSON is corrupted, you can restore the default configuration from the dashboard ("Restore profile" button).
ayuda.section8.a4_3: Double instance: Luna blocks multiple instances. If two instances write simultaneously, data may be overwritten.
ayuda.section9.title: Support
ayuda.section9.card_p: Luna is an independent project maintained in my free time. If you find it useful, consider buying me a coffee to help cover development, server, and testing costs.
ayuda.section9.footer: Report bugs or suggest improvements on GitHub Issues or by emailing support. All feedback is welcome.
